findings.description: E1 maps equip_copper_armor only to the family resolver findEquipmentAbility in BukkitRestrictionResolver. resolveArmorMaterialFamily has no 'copper_' branch, so resolveEquipmentAbility(copper_*) returns empty and that path can never guard copper. Every EquipmentAdapter route (interact, slot change, inventory click and drag, swap hands, dispenser, armor stand) therefore skips copper armor. The copper denial seen at runtime comes from the uncited native identity map (NativeEquipmentAbilities.java:12-14). The map is wrong for copper, and the Bukkit-layer gap is a latent risk on any route the native agent does not cover.

The group claims route and slot coverage, but each ability is tested only through right-click equip into the head slot (chest for elytra). The alternate canonical routes that the source guards are never runtime-proven: armor-slot click, shift-click and drag, hotbar swap, dispenser equip, and the other armor slots.

For the 6 working FAMILY abilities, E1 cites only the Bukkit EquipmentAdapter resolver. The tested denial (Item.use returns Pass) goes through the native Equippable.swapWithEquipmentSlot hook via NativeEquipmentAbilities, which E1 does not cite for them. BukkitRestrictionResolver.java also has no recorded hash in this E1; I verified it independently.

The probe reports the tested ability as null ("EQUIP_*": null) in every state line, so the server log never shows the lock state of this ability. Locked status follows only from count < threshold, which I confirmed against the raw config, and from the client overlay in rows.jsonl.

The client-mod path is stored with its Cyrillic folder name mojibake-encoded (UTF-8 bytes read as cp1251), so a third party cannot open it as written. I located the real file and its hash matches. This is a record defect only.
